transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I’m here because for the last couple of years, I just feel really low all the time. It’s like this heavy, empty feeling that doesn’t really ever lift. 

Even when I’m at work... I work as a quality inspector at a plant, just checking parts and weighing them as they come down the line. It's okay, I guess, but lately they've been making us fill out all these extra logging sheets because someone messed up a huge batch last month. It wasn't even my shift, it was the night shift, but we all have to pay for it now with all this extra paperwork. My supervisor Brenda is just constantly breathing down our necks about it, and she always uses this really loud voice that echoes across the whole floor... 

But, um, anyway, yeah. Even when I'm there, or at church, or just around people I care about, that heavy feeling is just always there. I just feel empty.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't know if I even pay attention to that anymore. I used to like going to the movies, I guess... back when I was taking a few classes at the community college, my roommate and I would go every Tuesday because it was discount night. 

They had this theater over by the mall with those big leather reclining seats? But the last time we went, my seat was actually broken. It got stuck halfway back, and the motor just kept making this awful whining noise every time I tried to fix it. And the guy sitting next to us had ordered nachos, and he was chewing so loud. Like, why would you get crunchy nachos for a quiet drama movie? It makes no sense. The cheese smelled really weird, too, kind of like... I don't know, burnt plastic? We ended up complaining to the teenager working the concession stand, but he didn't even know how to process a refund on the register. He had to call his manager, and the manager was on his dinner break, so we just stood there waiting for like twenty minutes... 

But, um... what were you asking me again? I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought.
Do you currently enjoy any activities?

I don't really know. Nothing really comes to mind. I guess I used to like reading, but I haven't picked up a book in months. My aunt gave me this huge hardcover for my birthday back in April, some kind of historical fiction thing set in the 1800s. She always gets me books because she used to be a librarian before she retired. 

She worked at the main branch downtown, the one with those huge stone lions out front? But they had to close it for a whole year because they found black mold in the basement. It was this whole big scandal because the city council had known about the leak for years and just kept putting off the repairs. My aunt was so mad about it, she wrote like three letters to the editor of the local paper. She actually got into a big argument with the mayor at a town hall meeting. 

But anyway... no, I don't really have anything I enjoy doing right now. It's just that heavy feeling all the time.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep?

Yeah, sleep is... it's a whole thing. Like, I'll be so completely exhausted after standing on the production floor all day, my feet just throbbing. We have these anti-fatigue mats, but they're so old and worn out that they don't even help anymore. Brenda said she put in an order for new ones back in January, but the purchasing department keeps kicking it back because of some budget freeze. It's ridiculous, they'll spend thousands on a new coffee machine for the front office—which, by the way, uses those little pods that are terrible for the environment—but they won't buy us decent mats. The guy who delivers the pods is always parking his truck right in the loading zone where we need to bring in the pallets, too. 

But um, yeah, when I finally get in bed, my mind just keeps running. I can't shut it off. I just think about everything I'm behind on, all the paperwork and everything. And even if I do manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself?

No... I don't really think about doing anything like that. I mean, I try to be careful. Not like some of the people at the plant. Last week, this guy Kyle actually cut his hand open on one of the sorting belts. It was this huge ordeal because they had to stop the entire line, and the safety coordinator had to come down from the third floor. 

The coordinator is this guy named Gary who wears these really thick glasses, and he always smells like strong peppermint? Like he eats those little red and white candies constantly, the ones you get at restaurants. He had this clipboard that was literally held together with silver duct tape, which is pretty ironic for a safety guy, if you think about it. Anyway, Kyle had to go to urgent care, and they made him take a drug test—which is standard policy, I guess—but he was completely freaking out because he went to some outdoor music festival over the weekend and... 

Um... wait, sorry. Did I answer your question? I wouldn't hurt myself, no.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite?

Um, yeah, my appetite is... it's really messed up. Most days I just skip eating entirely until my shift is almost over because nothing sounds good at all. Sometimes I'll just grab something from the vending machine in the breakroom when I'm completely drained. 

We actually just got a new vending machine last month because the old one kept eating everyone's quarters. It was this ancient thing with the coils that always got stuck. My coworker, Sarah, she lost like three dollars trying to get a bag of pretzels one time, and she actually shook the machine so hard the maintenance guy had to come yell at her. The maintenance guy is really nice, though, his name is Dave and he brings his golden retriever to work sometimes on the weekends. The dog's name is Buster and he loves belly rubs. 

But anyway, yeah, I just eat vending machine junk late in the day. And my weight has been going up and down so much because of it. Like, my work pants fit totally different from month to month. It's really frustrating.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

I don't think so? I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm always just trying to keep up with the sorting line, so I have to move pretty fast. Although, the line has been jamming a lot lately. The conveyor belt keeps snagging on this one metal bracket that got bent when the forklift bumped into it last Tuesday. 

The forklift driver is this guy Mike, and he was so apologetic about it. He actually bought donuts for the whole shift to make up for it. He got them from that bakery down on 4th Street, the one with the pink awning? They have these incredible maple bars, but they always sell out by 7 AM, so he must have gone really early. The lady who runs the bakery used to be a teacher at the high school I went to, actually. She taught chemistry, and she always wore these huge, colorful statement necklaces. She retired early to open the bakery because her husband got a job transfer or something. 

But um... what were you asking? Oh, moving slow. No, I don't think I'm moving or talking slower. Just feeling tired all the time.
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Guilty? Um... no, not really. I don't think I do anything that I need to feel guilty about, you know? I just go to work and come home. I mean, sometimes I feel bad when I can't cover a shift for someone. Like last week, Jessica asked me to cover for her because her daughter had a piano recital. 

Her daughter is like, eight, I think? She's learning to play that one song, the really famous one by Beethoven... Fur Elise! That's it. Jessica showed me a video of her practicing on her phone, and she was wearing this adorable little velvet dress with a white collar. It reminded me of a dress I had when I was little, except mine was navy blue and had these itchy lace sleeves that I hated. My mom made me wear it to my aunt's wedding, and the reception was at this weird country club that had a massive indoor fountain. Some kid actually dropped his toy car in the fountain and the staff had to fish it out with a pool skimmer. 

But, um... no, I don't really feel guilty about things. Just tired.
Do you feel like you've been fidgeting more than usual or having trouble sitting still?

Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any fidgeting or anything like that. I'm usually just sitting on the couch when I get home because I'm so exhausted. The couch is actually a hand-me-down from my older brother. He moved to Chicago for this tech job, and he didn't want to haul it all the way there. 

Chicago seems so cold, honestly. He sent me a picture of his car buried in snow last winter, and it looked miserable. He drives this little silver hatchback, and he had to dig it out with a shovel he borrowed from his neighbor. His neighbor is this older guy who apparently makes his own hot sauce and gives it out in little glass bottles. My brother said it's so spicy it makes his eyes water, but he puts it on everything anyway. He's always loved spicy food, even when we were kids. He used to put hot sauce on his scrambled eggs, which I always thought was so gross. I like my eggs just plain with a little salt and pepper. 

But, uh... fidgeting? No, I don't really do that. I'm mostly just too tired to move around a lot.
Do you think you've been talking more than usual lately?

Talking more? Um... no, I don't really think so. I actually feel like I barely talk at all these days, mostly just to the people on my shift when I have to. Like yesterday, I only really spoke to Sarah, who works the station next to mine. She was telling me about this new stray cat that started showing up on her porch. 

It's this scruffy orange tabby with a clipped ear, so she thinks it might be a catch-and-release cat from the shelter downtown. The shelter is right next to that old movie theater that closed down a few years ago. They used to show dollar movies on Tuesdays, and I remember going there with my friends in high school. We saw this terrible horror movie about a haunted mirror, and the popcorn was so stale it tasted like cardboard. But they had those really good cherry slushies that would turn your whole mouth red for the rest of the day. My friend Becca spilled one on her white jeans once, and she was so mad because she had just bought them from the mall with her birthday money. 

But um... no, I don't think I've been talking more. I'm usually just too drained to hold a conversation.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you happiness?

Pleasure? Um, I don't know... I guess I just don't really do much anymore to even know. I just go to work and come home. I work as an inspector at this manufacturing plant, checking these little metal parts as they come down the line. It's so repetitive, you know? Just looking at the same shiny little pieces of metal for hours. 

Sometimes the conveyor belt squeaks, and it drives me crazy. It sounds exactly like this squeaky wheel on the grocery cart I had last week at the supermarket. I was trying to buy some cereal, but the aisle was completely blocked by this huge display of paper towels. They were stacked up in the shape of a castle, which was kind of neat, but some kid had knocked over the top row. His mom looked so embarrassed, she was trying to stack them back up while holding a half-empty coffee cup. It was from that coffee shop on Main Street, the one with the green awning? They make a really good iced mocha, but they always put way too much whipped cream on top, and it melts over the side of the cup and makes your hands all sticky. 

But, um... happiness? I don't really know. I'm just tired all the time.
Do you feel like you're moving or acting more quickly than you used to?

Moving quickly? Um, no. Definitely not. If anything, I feel like I'm moving in slow motion most of the time. Like, the other day I actually missed my bus to work because I was just walking so slow. It's the number 42 bus, the one that goes past the old public library. The driver is this lady who always wears these giant, sparkly sunglasses, even when it's completely overcast and raining. I really don't know how she sees the road with those on. She told me once she got them at this huge flea market over in Westville. 

My mom used to take me to that flea market on weekends when I was little, and she'd buy me those cheap plastic rings that turn your fingers green. I had this one shaped like a dolphin that I wore every single day until the band finally snapped in half. Dolphins are supposed to be really smart, right? I saw this documentary on TV late one night where they were blowing these perfect bubble rings underwater and just playing with them. The ocean kind of terrifies me, though. It's so dark and deep, and you never really know what's swimming underneath you when you're out there. My cousin got stung by a jellyfish once when we went to the beach, and his leg swelled up so bad he couldn't even walk to the car. 

But, um... what were you asking? Oh, moving fast. No, I definitely don't do that. I just kind of drag myself everywhere.
Do you feel like your thoughts are slower than they used to be?

Slower thoughts? Um... I guess maybe? I don't really know if they're slower, exactly. It's more like everything is just kind of foggy up there. Like when you wake up from a nap and you don't know what time it is. I took a nap on Sunday afternoon, actually, right on the couch in the living room. The couch is this awful mustard yellow color that came with the apartment when I rented it. The landlord said it was vintage, but I'm pretty sure it's just old and stained. 

There's a stain on the middle cushion that looks exactly like the shape of Texas. I had to memorize all the states and capitals in fifth grade, and Mr. Henderson made us draw the map from memory. He was this really tall guy who always wore these horrible sweater vests, even in May when it was getting hot outside. He had this one with argyle print, green and brown, and he'd always get chalk dust all over the front of it. We used to clap the erasers outside for him against the brick wall of the school. The dust would fly everywhere and get in your hair, and it smelled so specific, you know? Like dry and dusty, kind of like the basement in my grandma's house. She used to keep all these jars of pickled beets down there on these wooden shelves that always looked like they were going to collapse. 

But um... thoughts. I don't know if they're slow. I just feel like it takes a lot of effort to think about anything right now.
Do you feel like it's an effort to initiate or complete everyday tasks?

Effort? Yeah... yeah, everything feels like a huge effort lately. Even just the small stuff at work, like filling out my inspection logs. I just stare at the clipboard, and it feels like it takes more energy than I actually have just to write the numbers down. We use these cheap blue pens at the plant, the kind where the ink always skips and you have to scribble on a scrap piece of paper to get it working again. I hate blue ink. I always preferred black ink, especially for writing. 

I used to love writing in these little notebooks when I was in high school. I had this one with a black cover that I covered in stickers I bought from the mall. The mall used to have this amazing pretzel place right next to the food court, and they sold these cinnamon sugar pretzels that were always perfectly warm. They'd hand them to you in this little white paper sleeve that would get grease spots all over it. I'd eat it while walking around the shoe store, looking at all the basketball sneakers. I used to drive to play basketball a lot, actually. But now... I don't know, even driving there feels like too much work. Just getting in the car and turning the key. 

Even washing my hair feels like a chore I just can't do. I bought this new shampoo last month, it smells like coconut and vanilla, which is supposed to be really relaxing. My roommate burns these vanilla candles all the time, and the wax always pools on the side of the glass jar. She has this whole collection of empty jars she says she's going to use for plants, but she never does. Plants are so much work, you know? You have to water them and make sure they get enough sun. I had a fern once, but it died after a week because I forgot to water it. 

But um, yeah, everything just takes so much energy. And even when I try to rest on my days off, it doesn't really refill me. I'm just always drained.
Do you feel like your body is heavier or harder to move than it used to be?

Heavier? I don't think so. I haven't really noticed feeling heavy, exactly. I mean, I weigh things all day on the sorting line at work, so I'm used to dealing with heavy stuff. We have these solid brass calibration weights for the digital scales, and the biggest one looks exactly like this doorstop we had in my dorm room back when I was taking classes at the community college. 

My roommate used to prop our door open with it all the time, hoping people would stop by and talk to us. She was always trying to make friends with everyone on our floor. There was this one guy across the hall who played acoustic guitar in the courtyard every single afternoon, but he only knew how to play, like, three songs. He played "Wonderwall" so much it drove me crazy. We actually went to a karaoke bar for my roommate's birthday and someone sang it there, too, completely off-key. That place was so gross, the floors were incredibly sticky, like they just mopped with soda instead of water. It smelled like stale beer and that cheap cherry air freshener, the kind shaped like a little tree that you hang from a rearview mirror. My dad used to have one of those in his old pickup truck. The truck was bright red and the heater in it never worked, so we'd freeze whenever he drove me to school in the winter... 

But wait, sorry, what were we talking about? My body feeling heavy? No, I don't think it feels heavier than normal. I just don't really have the energy to move it much.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're a burden to others?

Worthless? I don't... I don't know if worthless is the right word. I don't really think about it like that. But a burden? I mean, I guess I worry about that sometimes, but not... not all the time. I did feel like a burden when I had to ask my mom to help me move my mattress last month. It was this huge memory foam thing that came rolled up in a box, and when you cut the plastic, it expanded so fast. It was fascinating to watch, actually. 

We had to drag it up three flights of stairs because the elevator in my building has been broken since October. The maintenance guy put up this handwritten sign on neon pink paper that says "Out of Order," but the tape is peeling off the corners. He used that cheap clear tape that gets all yellow and brittle after a while. My aunt used to use that same tape to wrap all our Christmas presents, and she'd use way too much of it, so you'd have to use scissors just to open a gift. She always gave me the weirdest presents, too. Like one year she got me this ceramic frog that was supposed to hold a sponge next to the kitchen sink. It had these big, googly eyes painted on it, and the green paint was chipped right on its nose. I don't even use sponges, I prefer those plastic scrub brushes with the handles. You can put soap right in the handle and it dispenses when you push a button. It's so much more sanitary, you know? Sponges just hold onto all that bacteria and start smelling like mildew after two days...

But um... yeah, I don't really feel worthless, I don't think. I just don't have the energy to do much, so I guess I worry people think I'm lazy.
Do you feel like it's hard to think clearly or make decisions?

Hard to think clearly? I guess... I'm not really sure. I mean, making decisions is always kind of annoying anyway. Like yesterday, I was trying to decide what to have for lunch at the cafeteria at work. They had this meatloaf special, and the gravy looked so thick and gelatinous, kind of like that fake mud they use in movies. I saw this behind-the-scenes documentary once about how they make sound effects for movies, and they were squishing wet towels in a bucket to sound like someone walking through a swamp. It was so weird how they do that. 

They also showed how they make the sound of bones breaking by snapping celery stalks right next to the microphone. I buy celery sometimes because I tell myself I'm going to eat healthy and dip it in peanut butter, but it always just goes limp in the crisper drawer. My fridge makes this really loud humming noise whenever the compressor kicks on, and it vibrates the magnets I have on the door. I have this one magnet I got from a trip to the beach when I was ten, it's shaped like a dolphin but the tail broke off when I dropped it on the linoleum floor at my old apartment. That floor was awful, it had these weird yellow flowers printed on it that looked like they were straight out of the 1970s. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, decisions. I don't know, I don't really feel like I have a hard time thinking clearly. I just don't really want to think about much of anything right now.
Do you feel like your thoughts or movements are slower than they used to be?

Slower? Um... I don't really think so. I haven't noticed moving slower or anything. I mean, my job on the sorting line is pretty repetitive, so you just kind of get into a rhythm and do the same motions over and over. You really have to pay attention, though, because sometimes the conveyor belt jerks and things get backed up. Last week, it got stuck and made this horrible screeching noise, like metal scraping on metal. It sounded exactly like the brakes on my roommate's old Honda Civic. 

She drove that car until the engine practically blew up. The interior smelled like old french fries and wet dog, even though she didn't own a dog. She bought it used from this guy who lived out in the country, and he had these two massive golden retrievers that would just jump right into the backseat whenever he opened the door. I love dogs, but I can't have one in my apartment because the landlord is super strict about pets. He won't even let people have fish tanks because he's paranoid about water damage. Which is funny, because the pipes under my kitchen sink leak all the time anyway. I have to keep this plastic bucket under there, the kind you get ice cream in. It's one of those giant tubs of Neapolitan ice cream, but I only ever eat the chocolate and strawberry parts. The vanilla always gets left behind and gets all freezer-burned and icy...

Sorry, what was the question again? About moving slow? Yeah, no, I don't think I'm slower. I just... I just feel really tired all the time, so I don't do much.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to care about?

Lost interest? Um... I don't think so. I still like the same things, I guess. Like I still really like watching baking shows. I was watching this one last night where they had to make a cake that looked exactly like a pair of sneakers. It was crazy, they used all this fondant to make the shoelaces. Fondant always looks so smooth and perfect on TV, but it tastes like sweet plastic in real life. 

My cousin had a wedding cake completely covered in it, and nobody even ate the outside layer, they just peeled it off like a wrapper. Her wedding was outdoors in July, which was a terrible idea because the frosting underneath started melting in the sun. By the time they cut it, the whole cake was leaning to one side like the Leaning Tower of Pisa. I actually did a project on the Leaning Tower of Pisa in middle school. We had to build a structural model out of popsicle sticks, and I used so much hot glue that I got a second-degree burn on my thumb. The blister took like three weeks to heal, and I couldn't play my Nintendo DS properly the whole time. I had the metallic pink one, and I was obsessed with this game where you had to train virtual puppies. You actually had to speak into the little microphone on the console to teach them tricks, so I'd be sitting in the back of my mom's minivan just yelling "Sit! Roll over!" at a screen. My older brother thought it was the most annoying thing in the world, so he used to hide the stylus from me. He would put it on top of the refrigerator where I couldn't reach it... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, losing interest in things. Yeah, no, I don't think I've lost interest. I still care about the stuff I used to. I just... I don't really do much with my time right now, I guess.
Do you feel like you're unable to concentrate on things?

Concentrate? Um... I don't know. I guess I can concentrate fine when I need to. Like at work, you really have to focus when you're inspecting the parts coming down the line. If you miss a defect, it messes up the whole batch. Last Tuesday, this guy on the shift before me missed a huge crack in one of the plastic casings, and the supervisor was yelling so loud you could hear him over the machinery. 

The supervisor has this really booming voice, kind of like a radio announcer. It reminds me of the guy who used to do the announcements at my high school football games. I never really liked football, but I went to the games because they sold these amazing soft pretzels at the concession stand. They were always super warm and covered in those giant chunks of salt. I tried making soft pretzels at home once, but I didn't realize you had to boil the dough in baking soda water before you bake them. It sounded like a weird science experiment, so I just skipped that step, and they came out tasting like really dense, salty bread rolls. I ended up feeding most of them to the pigeons at the park near my apartment. There's this one pigeon that's always there, it's missing a toe on its left foot and has these really iridescent purple and green feathers on its neck. I read somewhere that pigeons actually have really good memories and can recognize human faces, which is kind of creepy if you think about it. Imagine a bird holding a grudge against you because you didn't give it enough bread...

Oh, wait. Concentrate. Sorry, I lost track. No, I don't think I have trouble concentrating. I just... I don't really have the energy to focus on much lately.

patient.answer:
Yeah, sleep is... it's a whole thing. Like, I'll be so completely exhausted after standing on the production floor all day, my feet just throbbing. We have these anti-fatigue mats, but they're so old and worn out that they don't even help anymore. Brenda said she put in an order for new ones back in January, but the purchasing department keeps kicking it back because of some budget freeze. It's ridiculous, they'll spend thousands on a new coffee machine for the front office—which, by the way, uses those little pods that are terrible for the environment—but they won't buy us decent mats. The guy who delivers the pods is always parking his truck right in the loading zone where we need to bring in the pallets, too.
